title: The largest animal that ever existed is alive right now
origin: Superlative-formula #2, from the topic bench (research/video-notes/topic-0006-stitches.md, score lane 'largest animal that ever existed'). Day-021 queue directive: option (b) — the next short goes for a bolder-composition world; one dominant object (the whale spans the frame in every scene). Script, drawings and audio are original.

hook.narration: The largest animal ever recorded is no dinosaur. It's alive right now.

visual.v1: Whale silhouette, huge, crosses the whole frame left-to-right under the title; the tail breaks the surface at the end.

scenes.narration: The blue whale tops two hundred tonnes — thirty-three elephants in one body.

visual.v1: Whale mid-frame; six elephants stand on its back as a stamp counts 33.

scenes.narration: It grows as long as three school buses.

visual.v1: Three yellow buses nose-to-tail along the whale's flank, dimension line.

scenes.narration: Its tongue alone weighs as much as an elephant.

visual.v1: Zoom: mouth slightly open, tongue out flat, one elephant standing on it.

scenes.narration: Its heart weighs four hundred pounds — three grown men.

visual.v1: Chest goes x-ray; four-chambered heart + aorta arch; three stickmen for scale.

scenes.narration: The artery leaving it is wide enough for a newborn to crawl through.

visual.v1: Aorta ring close-up; a crawling newborn figure inches through it.

scenes.narration: A calf is born weighing two and a half tonnes.

visual.v1: Calf glides beside the mother's flank; size plates tick on.

scenes.narration: Then it gains ninety kilograms a day, on milk alone.

visual.v1: Calf silhouette inflates on a counter; milk stream lines from the mother.

scenes.narration: But the biggest animal on Earth eats one of the smallest.

visual.v1: Wide shot: the whale dwarfed by a drifting krill cloud the size of a city block.

scenes.narration: Four tonnes of krill a day — each one smaller than your thumb.

visual.v1: Krill close-up: one krill vs a thumb outline; counter ticks to 4 T.

scenes.narration: No teeth — it lunges, and strains the swarm through baleen.

visual.v1: The lunge: mouth yawns open, krill+water in, baleen comb strains, water jets out.

scenes.narration: The dinosaurs never held the record. The champion is out there right now.

visual.v1: Whale silhouette crosses back under the title; loop target = frame 0.

sources.wwf: WWF blue whale facts (worldwildlife.org/resources/facts/whats-the-biggest-animal-that-has-ever-lived-and-other-blue-whale-facts): biggest animal ever incl. dinosaurs; up to 100 ft = three school buses; up to 200 tons = as heavy as about 33 elephants; nearly 8,000 lb of krill a day
sources.heart2015: National Geographic Education blog, 2015-08-31 (blog.education.nationalgeographic.org/2015/08/31/how-big-is-a-blue-whales-heart): first preserved blue whale heart (2015 ROM dissection) ~400 lb, 5 ft x 4 ft x 5 ft; the researcher's golf-cart quote noted as NOT really true (heart smaller than folklore) — we use the measured 400 lb, rendered as three 60-kg men
sources.aorta2015: Korea Times 2015-09-14 report on the same 2015 Royal Ontario Museum dissection: the aorta is large enough for a human baby/child to crawl through
sources.aad: Australian Antarctic Division (antarctica.gov.au/about-antarctica/animals/whales/blue-whale, updated 2024-12): newborn calf ~2.5 t, can put on ~100 kg/day late in suckling
sources.adfg: Alaska Department of Fish & Game, baleen whale birth & care: nursing blue whale calves gain ~90 kg (200 lb) per day
sources.tongue: Monterey Bay Aquarium + BBC Discover Wildlife (2025): a blue whale's tongue weighs over 3 t — about as much as an elephant
sources.noaa4t: NOAA/NPS blue whale pages: feeding-season intake up to ~4 tonnes of krill per day (WWF: nearly 8,000 lb)
